workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§169–169
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §169: The Herdsmen Who Warned Chinggis
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§169–169, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: One section. Jeke-Chelen, coming home from the meeting that agreed to seize Temüjin the next morning, says so to his wife; she scolds him, and the herdsman Badai, bringing milk, hears and goes to tell his fellow herdsman Kishiliq. Kishiliq goes to listen and finds Narin-Kegen, Jeke-Chelen's son, telling his own herdsman to tie up two horses for a night ride. The two herdsmen take the horses and ride through the night to Chinggis Qahan to warn him. Several passages are marked in the notes as first readings.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Tein bučižu barija keġen üge baralduγsan-i Atan-u deġü Jeke-Čelen ger-tür(i)-jen irežü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to surround (stem inferred from Ming 圍) [圍着]

words.reading: 把舌剌勒都︀黑撒泥 baralduγsan-i

morph.gloss: to settle together, agree [商議定了的 行]
Atan, a man's name (personal name) [人名的]
Jeke-Chelen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: So, surrounding, let-us-seize, saying, word agreed-on-(object), Atan-of younger-brother Jeke-Čelen, own-home-to coming, saying:
sentences.i: Jeke-Chelen, Atan's younger brother, came to his own home, speaking of the word they had agreed on, 'So, let us surround and seize him':
sentences.n: The first words are a back-reference: Tein bučižu barija keġen üge, 'the word that says "so, surrounding, let us seize"', is the word agreed on, baralduγsan-i (baraldu- 'settle together' + past participle -γsan 'what was settled' + accusative -i; Ming 商議定了的 行). The accusative makes it the object of ügülerün 'saying', so the agreed word is what he speaks of; what he actually says follows in the next units. Atan-u deġü is 'Atan's younger brother' (genitive first; Ming 人名的 弟). ger-tür(i)-jen is ger 'home' + dative-locative -tür + reflexive-possessive -(i)jen 'his own' (Ming 家 自的行); irežü is 'coming'. bučižu is 'surrounding', but the stem buči- is inferred from the Ming 圍 alone. The Ming gives only 人名 'a man's name' for Atan and for Jeke-Čelen. A Jeke-Chelen/Jeke-Cheren is a Tatar in §§154–157; nothing here shows that he is the same man, and I do not assume it.

sentences.t: "Manaγar erte Temüžin-i barija keġeldübe.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名 行]

sentences.l: "Tomorrow early Temüžin-(object) let-us-seize, said-together.
sentences.i: "Tomorrow, early, let us seize Temüjin. So we agreed.
sentences.n: This is the start of what Jeke-Chelen says; Shiratori's quotation mark opens at Manaγar and is not closed until the end of the unit-3 speech, so it runs on into the next unit. His hearer is not named here (his wife answers him in unit 4). manaγar erte is 'tomorrow, early' (Ming 明 早). Temüžin-i has the accusative -i (Ming 行) and is the object of barija, bari- 'seize' + -ja 'let us' (the Ming 拿咱 has 咱 'let us'). keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- 'together' + past -be (Ming 共說了): 'we said it to one another', that is, agreed. The Mongol has no subject; 'we' is from the reciprocal and from his having been at the agreement.

sentences.t: "Ene üge-ji Temüžin-e kelen kürgen odqu küġün-i ambar ele bolγaγdaju" keġe- žüġüi.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名 行]
to say (first half of keġe-žüġüi, split at the line end) [說]

sentences.l: This word Temüžin-to word bringing going person-(object) how only be-made," said.
sentences.i: This word, and the man who is to go and deliver word of it to Temüjin: how is that to be arranged?" he said.
sentences.n: A hard sentence; this is a first reading. The speech from unit 2 goes on and closes at 'said': the split keġe- / žüġüi (Ming 說 / 了) is just 'said'. The clause ends ambar ele bolγaγdaju, 'how, (only/indeed), be made' (Ming 怎生 但 被做有): bol- 'become' + causative -γa- + passive -γda- ('be made'), with an ending -ju I cannot place. Before it stand two objects with -i/-ji (Ming 行): ene üge-ji 'this word' and odqu küġün-i 'the person who goes' (od- 'go' + participle -qu, Ming 去的), with Temüžin-e kelen kürgen 'bringing word to Temüjin' (Ming 送) before it. The Mongol has no word for 'who'; the question is carried by ambar 'how'. Two readings are open: 'who is to be sent to him?' or 'what is to be done about anyone who might go to him?'. The English leaves it open and the Ming does not decide.

sentences.t: Tein ügüleküi-dür eme in-ü Alaγčid ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Alaqchid, probably a woman's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.l: So, saying-when, wife his Alaγčid, saying:
sentences.i: When he had said this, his wife Alaqchid said:
sentences.n: ügüleküi-dür is ügüle- 'speak' + participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, 'at the speaking', so 'when he said' (Ming 說的 行); verb + -küi-dür as 'when' comes again in unit 6. eme in-ü is 'his wife', the genitive in-ü standing after its noun (Ming 妻 他的). Alaγčid is for the Ming only 人名 'a man's name'; as the wife's name I take it to be a woman's. The speaker of ügüleküi-dür is Jeke-Chelen, since his wife answers him. The house spelling of γ as q gives Alaqchid.

sentences.t: "Tere deleme üge čin-u jaγ̇un bolumui. Haran ba ünemigeġüžei" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: loose, unrestrained (Ming 泛濫 'overflowing'; elsewhere 'rashly, hastily') [泛濫]
to be true, sincere (stem inferred from Ming 做眞誠 and ünen 'true') [做眞誠]

sentences.l: "That loose word your what is? People also be-sincere-(let/may)," said.
sentences.i: "That loose talk of yours, what is it? Let the people be sincere as well," she said.
sentences.n: tere deleme üge is 'that loose word': deleme is Ming 泛濫 'overflowing, indiscriminate' (the glossary has 'rashly, hastily' for it from another place), and it stands before üge as an adjective. čin-u is 'your' (či 'you', genitive on the stem čin-), and jaγ̇un bolumui 'what is it?' (Ming 甚麽 做有; -umui is the present ending). The last clause is a puzzle and I give it only as the Ming reads: haran ba ünemigeġüžei is 'people also make-sincere/true' (Ming 人 也 做眞誠), ünemige- being a stem drawn from the Ming and from ünen 'true', with an ending -ġüžei that I take as optative ('let'). What she means I cannot tell. Perhaps 'the people too should be sincere', perhaps 'people too will take it for true'; the English follows the first only for want of better.

sentences.t: Tein keleleküi-dür aduγ̇uči in-ü Badai sün kürgere irežü ene ene üge-ji sonosču qariba.

morph.gloss: Badai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
ending of uncertain force, perhaps a converb: -ing (Ming 來 'hither')

sentences.l: So, saying-when, horse-herder his Badai fresh-mare's-milk bringing coming, this this word hearing, turned-back.
sentences.i: While this was being said, Badai, his horse-herder, who had come bringing mare's milk, heard these words and went back.
sentences.n: keleleküi-dür (Ming 說的 時) is kelele- 'speak' (kele 'tongue' + verb-maker -le-) + -küi + -dür, 'at the speaking', the same pattern as in unit 4 with another verb. It does not say who speaks; it follows the wife's speech, so the English says 'this'. aduγ̇uči in-ü Badai is 'his horse-herder Badai' (in-ü after its noun; Ming 放馬的 他的); whose herder he is is not stated (presumably Jeke-Chelen's). sün is mare's milk (Ming 生馬妳子), and kürgere irežü 'bringing, coming' (Ming 送來 來着), where the shape of -re is uncertain. ene ene is printed twice and glossed twice (這 這); I keep both in the words and in 'l' and say 'these words' once. qariba is qari- 'turn back' + -ba (Ming 囘了).

sentences.t: Badai jorčižu nökör aduγ̇uči Kišiliγ-a Čeren-ü ügülegsen üges ügüležüġü.

morph.gloss: Badai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]
Cheren (perhaps Jeke-Cheren), a man's name (personal name) [人名的]

sentences.l: Badai going, companion horse-herder Kišiliγ-to, Čeren-of said words spoke.
sentences.i: Badai went and told Kishiliq, his fellow horse-herder, the words Cheren had spoken.
sentences.n: nökör aduγ̇uči Kišiliγ-a is 'to the companion, the horse-herder Kishiliq' (Ming 伴當 放馬的 人名行); -a is the dative-locative (Ming 行). Čeren-ü ügülegsen üges is 'the words spoken by Cheren': ügülegsen the past participle (Ming 說了的), üges the plural (Ming 言語每). The speaker is Čelen in unit 1 and Čeren here; the Ming has 人名 for each and the Han differ in 舌 (which writes r) and in the last syllables (連 against 列). The story needs one man, so I treat them as one; Shiratori's l/r is kept in the Mongol and the English uses Cheren, as in §§154–157.

sentences.t: Kišiliγ ügülerün: "Bi basa odču uqasuγai" keġežü ger-tür odčuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to understand, find out (stem inferred from Ming 察聽 'look into, listen') [察聽咱]

sentences.l: Kišiliγ saying: "I again going, let-me-find-out," saying, home-to went.
sentences.i: Kishiliq said, "I will go again and find out," and went to the tent.
sentences.n: Bi basa odču is 'I, again, going' (Ming 我 再 去着). uqasuγai is uqa- 'understand' (a stem drawn from the Ming 察聽 'inquire, listen') + -suγai, the first-person optative 'let me' (the Ming adds 咱, as the glossary has 'may I' for it). ger-tür is 'to the tent/home', as in unit 1 without the reflexive. odčuγ̇ui is od- 'go' + past -čuγ̇ui (Ming 去了; the ending's analysis is uncertain). Whose tent it is is not said. The next unit has Cheren's son sitting outside, so it is probably Cheren's; that is an inference.

sentences.t: Čeren-ü köġün Narin-Keġen γada saγ̇užu sumud(i)-jan hürün saγ̇užu ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Cheren, a man's name (personal name) [人名的]
Narin-Kegen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to whet, polish (stem inferred from Ming 磋 'to grind, polish') [磋]

sentences.l: Čeren-of son Narin-Keġen outside sitting, own-arrows polishing sitting, saying:
sentences.i: Cheren's son Narin-Kegen was sitting outside, sitting there polishing his own arrows, and said:
sentences.n: Čeren-ü köġün Narin-Keġen is 'Cheren's son Narin-Kegen' (possessor first). γada saγ̇užu is 'outside, sitting' (Ming 外面 坐着). sumud(i)-jan is sumu 'arrow' + plural -d + -(i)jan 'his own' (Ming 箭(每) 自的行); the bracketed (i) is Shiratori's and may be the accusative (Ming 行), 'his own arrows' as object of hürün. hürün is hürü- (a stem drawn from the Ming 磋, 'to grind, polish') + converb -n. The doubled saγ̇užu is as printed.

sentences.t: "Tuγar bida jaγ̇u keġeldüleġei. Kele-ben abdaqun; ken-ü ama idqaqun" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: ending of unclear force (Ming 的); read 'is …ed'
to stop, check (stem inferred from Ming 止) [止當的]
ending of unclear force (Ming 當的 'ought'); read 'is to be …ed'

sentences.l: "Just-now we what said-together? Own-speech to-be-taken, whose mouth to-be-stopped?" said.
sentences.i: "What have we just been saying to one another? Our own talk is being taken; whose mouth is to be stopped?" he said.
sentences.n: This is Narin-Kegen's speech; no hearer is named (unit 11 has him speak to Kishiliq 'again'). tuγar bida jaγ̇u keġeldüleġei is 'just now we, what, said together' (Ming 恰纔 咱 甚 共說來): bida is 'we' including the hearer (Ming 咱), keġeldü- the reciprocal, and -leġei an ending marked 來 by the Ming (force uncertain). kele-ben is 'own speech' (Ming 話 自的行, reflexive -ben). abdaqun is ab- 'take' + passive -da- + -qun (Ming 被取的); idqaqun is idqa- 'stop' (a stem drawn from the Ming 止) + -qun (Ming 止當的, where 當 means 'ought'). The ending -qun is not explained; I read the first as 'is taken' and the second, from 當, as 'is to be stopped'. ken-ü ama is 'whose mouth' (Ming 誰的 口). What 'taken' means is open ('overheard' is a guess from the scene).

sentences.t: Tein kēġed Narin-Keġen basa aduγ̇uči-daγ̇dan Kišiliγ-a ügülerün:

morph.gloss: converb: having … (written together with the stem as a long ē)
Narin-Kegen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
dative-locative with reflexive-possessive: to one's own (uncertain)
Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]

sentences.l: So said-having, Narin-Keġen again his-own-horse-herder Kišiliγ-to saying:
sentences.i: Having said that, Narin-Kegen spoke again to Kishiliq, his own horse-herder:
sentences.n: kēġed is keġe- 'say' + converb -ġed, run together with the stem and written with a long ē (Ming 說了): 'having said'. aduγ̇uči-daγ̇dan Kišiliγ-a is 'to his own horse-herder, to Kishiliq' (Ming 放馬的 自的行, 人名行). The ending -daγ̇dan is uncertain: a dative-locative with a reflexive-possessive is a guess from the Ming 自的行. So Kishiliq is Narin-Kegen's own herder, which fits his being called a horse-herder in unit 7.

sentences.t: "Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an, Aman-Čaγaγ̇an- Keġer qojar-i barižu abčira. Hujažu süni erte morilaqu" keġežüġüi.

words.reading: 篾舌兒乞歹-察(中合)安 Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an

morph.gloss: Merkidai-Chaqa'an, a horse's name (Ming 馬名) [馬名]
Aman-Chaqa'an, first half of the horse's name Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer, split at the line end [馬]
Keger, second half of the horse's name Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer (keġer is 'steppe' elsewhere, Ming 野; here the Ming says only 名) [名]
to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; form uncertain); bare stem: bring! [將來]
to mount a horse (mori 'horse' + verb-maker -la-; Ming 上馬) [上馬我]
future participle: I shall … (Ming 我; uncertain)

sentences.l: "Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two-(object) seizing bring. Tying, night early I-will-mount," said.
sentences.i: "Seize the two horses Merkidai-Chaqa'an and Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger and bring them. Tie them up. I shall ride early in the night," he said.
sentences.n: Two names, Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an and Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer (Ming 馬名 'a horse's name'); the second is split over a line (Aman-Čaγaγ̇an- / Keġer). I leave them untranslated: Merkid is a people and čaγaγan 'white' elsewhere, but here the Ming says only 'horse' and 'name'. qojar-i is 'the two' with the accusative (Ming 兩箇行), the object of barižu abčira, 'seizing, bring!': abčira is a bare stem used as a command (Ming 將來; form uncertain). hujažu 'tying' (Ming 拴着) is a converb in form; I read it as a command too from the run of the sentence. süni erte morilaqu is 'night, early, I will mount': morila- 'mount a horse' (mori) + -qu (Ming 上馬我). 'Early in the night' is my rendering; it could equally be 'at night, early (before dawn)'.

sentences.t: Kišiliγ jorčižu Badai-(j)a ügü- lerün: "Tuγar-un kelen čin-u bolγaγ̇aba maγad bolba.

morph.gloss: Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Badai, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]
to speak (first half of ügü-lerün, split at the line end) [說]
verb-maker -le- and converb of time -rün (second half of ügü-lerün)
to verify, check (Ming 體覆; perhaps bol- 'become' + a causative; form uncertain) [體覆了]

sentences.l: Kišiliγ going, Badai-to saying: "Just-now-of word your was-verified, truly became.
sentences.i: Kishiliq went to Badai and said, "What you said just now has been verified; it has truly come about.
sentences.n: Kišiliγ jorčižu Badai-(j)a ügü- lerün: 'Kishiliq, going, to Badai, saying', the verb split ügü- / lerün across the line and -(j)a the dative-locative (Ming 行). tuγar-un kelen čin-u is 'your word of just now' (tuγar 'just now' + genitive, Ming 恰纔; čin-u 'your'); it can only be what Badai reported in unit 7. bolγaγ̇aba (Ming 體覆了, 'examined, verified') I cannot parse closely: bol- 'become' with a causative and past -ba is a guess, so the exact sense is uncertain. maγad bolba is 'truly became, came to pass' (Ming 眞實 做了). I read it as 'Badai's report has proved true'; the Mongol does not say how Kishiliq knows, but the preceding scene is his visit to Narin-Kegen.

sentences.t: Edöġe bida qojar Temüžin-e kelen kürgen jorčija" keġen üge baraldužu Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an, Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer qojar-i barižu irežü hujažu

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名 行]
to settle together, agree (stem inferred from Ming 議定) [議定着]

words.reading: 篾舌兒乞歹-察(中合)安 Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an

morph.gloss: Merkidai-Chaqa'an, a horse's name (Ming 馬名) [馬名]

words.reading: 阿蠻-察(中合)安-客額舌兒 Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer

glyphs.s: 阿蠻-察(中合)安-客額舌兒

morph.gloss: Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger, a horse's name (Ming 馬名) [馬名]

sentences.l: Now we two Temüžin-to word bringing let-us-go," saying word agreeing, Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two-(object) seizing coming tying,
sentences.i: Now let us two go and deliver word to Temüjin," and, agreeing on this word, they seized the two horses Merkidai-Chaqa'an and Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger, brought them and tied them up,
sentences.n: The speech begun in unit 13 closes here, at jorčija": edöġe bida qojar is 'now we two' (Ming 如今 咱 兩箇) and Temüžin-e kelen kürgen jorčija 'to Temüjin, word bringing, let us go' (Ming 送, 去咱; jorči- + -ja 'let us', as barija in unit 1). keġen üge baraldužu is 'the word saying …, agreeing', as in unit 1 (keġen üge) with the converb of the same verb baraldu- (Ming 議定着): they agree on this word. Then the chain barižu irežü hujažu 'seizing, coming, tying' (Ming 拿着 來着 拴着) takes the two named horses, qojar-i (Ming 兩箇 行), as in unit 12. The Mongol does not say whose horses they are; they are the ones Narin-Kegen named, which is an inference. The converb chain runs on, nine converbs in all, to kürčü in unit 17; it is cut here and in units 15 and 16 at readable points.

sentences.t: üdeši büġed Qos-tur(i)-jan nigen quriγa-ban alažu iseri-jer-en bolγažu

morph.gloss: house (Ming 房子; stem and sense uncertain) [房子 自的行]
bed, frame (Ming 床; what object is meant is uncertain) [床 敎自的行]
instrumental: with (Ming 敎 glosses instrumentals elsewhere)

sentences.l: Evening then own-house-in one own-lamb killing, own-frame-with making-done,
sentences.i: In the evening, in their own house, they killed one lamb of their own and cooked it through with their own 'frame',
sentences.n: üdeši büġed is 'evening, then' (Ming 晩夕 便; büġed is a particle marking the next step). Qos-tur(i)-jan: the stem qos is uncertain, taken from the Ming 房子 'house'; -tur is the dative-locative, -(i)jan 'own' (Ming 自的行), 'in/to their own house'. nigen quriγa-ban alažu is 'one own-lamb, killing' (Ming 一箇 羔兒 殺着), quriγa with the reflexive -ban. iseri-jer-en is iseri (Ming 床, 'bed, frame') + -jer, the instrumental (the Ming 敎 glosses instrumentals elsewhere) + -en, 'own'; I do not know what a cooking 'bed' would be, and 'spit' would be a guess, so I give 'frame' in quotes. bolγažu is bol- + causative -γa- + -žu, 'making become', here 'cooking until done' (Ming 煮熟着).

sentences.t: Merkidai- Čaγaγ̇an, Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer qojar belen hujaγsad-i unužu süni-de jorčižu

morph.gloss: first half of the horse's name Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an, split at the line end [馬]
Chaqa'an, second half of the horse's name Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an (Ming 名) [名]

words.reading: 阿蠻-察(中合)安-客額舌兒 Aman-Čaγaγ̇an-Keġer

glyphs.s: 阿蠻-察(中合)安-客額舌兒

morph.gloss: Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger, a horse's name (Ming 馬名) [馬名]
ready, at hand (Ming 見 read as 'present'; sense uncertain) [見]
past participle, plural: those that were …

sentences.l: Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two ready tied-ones-(object) riding, by-night going,
sentences.i: mounted the two horses, Merkidai-Chaqa'an and Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger, that they had kept ready tied, and rode off by night,
sentences.n: The first horse-name is split across the line (Merkidai- / Čaγaγ̇an). belen is Ming 見, which I read in its colloquial sense 'at hand, ready' rather than 'seen' (uncertain). hujaγsad-i is huja- 'tie' + the plural of the past participle -γsad 'those that were tied' + accusative -i (Ming 拴着的 行). unužu is 'riding' (Ming 騎着), süni-de 'by night' (dative-locative; Ming 夜裏 行, as in the published parts) and jorčižu 'going'. The pair is the one of units 12 and 14.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur süni kürčü ger-ün ümerēče Badai, Kišiliγ qojar ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin [太祖︀]
Badai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan-to night arriving, tent-of from-behind Badai, Kišiliγ two saying:
sentences.i: They reached Chinggis Qahan in the night, and from behind the tent Badai and Kishiliq, the two, spoke:
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur is 'to Chinggis Qahan' (Ming 太祖 皇帝行), dative-locative -dur on the title. süni kürčü is 'arriving by night' (kür- 'reach' + -čü; Ming 夜裏 到着). ger-ün ümerēče is 'from behind the tent' (Ming 房的 北處, literally 'the tent's north place', perhaps the back of the tent): ger-ün is the genitive, ümer 'behind' takes the ablative -ēče. The phrase could go with kürčü ('arrived from behind the tent') or with ügülerün ('spoke from behind the tent'); I attach it to the speaking. qojar 'the two' (Ming 兩箇) follows the pair; the 'two' is the Ming's.

morph.gloss: Merkidai-Chaqa'an, a horse's name (Ming 馬名) [馬名]

glyphs.s: 阿蠻-察(中合)安-客額舌兒

to tie, fasten; bare stem: tie! [拴]

sentences.l: Jeke-Čeren-of said words, son-(object) his Narin-Keġen-of arrows polishing sitting said-(object), Merkidai-Čaγaγan, Aman-Čaγaγan-Keġer two geldings seizing tie said words, all-(object) saying gave.
sentences.i: The words that Jeke-Cheren had spoken, and what his son Narin-Kegen said as he sat polishing his own arrows, 'Seize the two geldings Merkidai-Chaqa'an and Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger and tie them,' all those words they told him.
sentences.n: A long sentence that reports what the two said, not their exact words. Shiratori's quotation marks open before Jeke-Čeren-ü and before Merkidai-Čaγaγ̇an and are not closed until the mark after baralduba in unit 21, so I do not treat them as one literal speech; the English sets only Narin-Kegen's order in single quotes, since it is plainly what he said. Jeke-Čeren-ü ügülegsen üges is 'the words said by Jeke-Cheren'; köġün-i in-ü Narin-Keġen-(n)ü … ügülegsen-i is '(the words) of his son Narin-Kegen, said sitting polishing his own arrows' (Ming 子 行 他的 人名的 … 說來的 行). The accusative on köġün-i and on ügülegsen-i is the Ming's 行; why köġün is accusative I cannot say. -(n)ü is the genitive after an n-final name, in the front-vowel form that matches Keġen (the (n) is Shiratori's). aγtas is 'geldings' (aγta + plural -s; Ming 騸馬每): the two named horses again, here called geldings. huja 'tie!' is a bare stem (Ming 拴); keġegsen üges 'the words said' (Ming 說來的 言語每); bügüde-ji 'all' with the accusative (Ming 都 行); ügüležü ögbe 'telling, gave' (Ming 說着 與了), which I take as 'told them to him'.

sentences.t: Basa Badai, Kišiliγ qojar ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Badai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Kishiliq, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Again Badai, Kišiliγ two saying:
sentences.i: Again Badai and Kishiliq, the two, said:
sentences.n: basa is 'again' (Ming 再); qojar 'the two' follows the pair (Ming 兩箇); ügülerün is 'saying'. This is the formula that introduces a speech.

sentences.t: "Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i sojurγaγ̇asu arijal ügei bi.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin [太祖︀]

words.reading: 莎余舌兒中合阿速 sojurγaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜呵]

sentences.l: "Čiṅgis Qaγan-(object) if-favouring, doubt without is.
sentences.i: "If (someone) favours Chinggis Qahan, there is no doubt.
sentences.n: A doubtful sentence; a first reading. sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'show favour, bestow a grace' (Ming 恩賜) + the conditional -γ̇asu 'if' (Ming 呵). Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i carries the accusative -i (Ming 皇帝行), so by grammar the Qahan is the object of the favour, 'if (one) favours Chinggis Qahan', and the Mongol names no one who does the favouring. The Ming 行 is loose enough to mean 'to', so the sense may be nearer 'if favour is shown to Chinggis Qahan'; I could not settle it and the English follows the accusative. arijal ügei bi is 'there is no doubt' (Ming 疑 無 有; ügei 'without', bi 'is'). The quotation mark before Čiṅgis opens the speech that closes in the next unit.

sentences.t: Bučižü barija keġen üge baralduba" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to surround (stem inferred from Ming 圍) [圍着]
to settle together, agree [共議定了]

sentences.l: Surrounding, let-us-seize, saying, word agreed," said.
sentences.i: 'Surrounding him, let us seize him': that is the word they agreed on," they said.
sentences.n: The quotation opened in the last unit closes here at baralduba". bučižü barija keġen üge baralduba is 'the word "surrounding, let us seize" was agreed': bučižü 'surrounding', barija 'let us seize', keġen üge 'the word saying', baralduba 'they agreed' (Ming 共議定了), the same words and the same verb baraldu- as in unit 1, where the participle baralduγsan-i stood. The subject is unmarked; I take it to be the plotters. keġebe 'said' (Ming 說了) ends §169, which closes where it began, on the plan.
